decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 50 basis points, to 4.75% to 5%. The vote was 11-1. Dissenting: Michelle W. Bowman.

changes.quote: Job gains have slowed, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains have moderated, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low.”

changes.quote: Inflation has made further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent objective but remains somewhat elevated.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In recent months, there has been some further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective.”

changes.quote: Inflation has eased over the past year but remains somewhat elevated.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: The Committee has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent, and judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals continue to move into better balance.”

changes.quote: In light of the progress on inflation and the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point to 4-3/4 to 5 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.”

changes.quote: In considering additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In considering any adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the …”

tone_quotes.quote: In light of the progress on inflation and the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point to 4-3/4 to 5 percent.
Job gains have slowed, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low.
The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 21.51% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.7% and moved +5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.35% would rise by about $9.81 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 4.2%, and employers added an average of 50k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.6% over the past year (August 2024); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +2 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.29%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.03% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 46%, cut 54%, hike 0%.
